cover.headline: A well-run cash machine whose growth has shrunk to 3-4%: the price still assumes the AI de-rating will reverse
cover.lead: HCLTech is India's third-largest IT services company (US$14.7 bn revenue in FY26, 2.2 lakh people), controlled by the Nadar family (60.9%). It has been the fastest-growing tier-1 Indian IT firm for three years, yet growth keeps falling: +5.4%, +4.7% and +3.9% in constant currency in FY24-26, FY27 guided at 1-4% and +2.6% YoY in Q1FY27. Bookings are strong (record Q1 TCV of US$2.4 bn plus a US$1.14 bn mega deal) and Advanced AI revenue grew 62%, but management itself expects AI to deflate its traditional work by 2-3% a year. The street values HCLTech on **P/E on FY28E EPS (15-19x)**. Our EPS of ₹72.6 (FY27E) and ₹77.0 (FY28E) is in line with the street; FY27's +18% is mostly the weaker rupee. Applying **13x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹78.6** (its 19.8x median forward P/E since 2021, cut by the IT sector's 34% de-rating) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,035, DCF ₹1,296. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}. A ~5.6% dividend yield softens, but does not close, the gap.

arguments.h: Growth has converged down to the pack
arguments.p: Constant-currency growth: 13.7% (FY23), 5.4% (FY24), 4.7% (FY25), 3.9% (FY26); FY27 guidance 1-4% and Q1 +2.6%. Two big US telecom clients cut spend, ERS fell 3.7% QoQ and HCLSoftware shrank 5.3%. In dollars we forecast +2.9% / +3.9% / +3.7% for FY27-29E.

arguments.h: AI cuts both ways, and the cut is bigger today
arguments.p: Advanced AI revenue is US$171 m a quarter (+62% YoY) but only ~4.7% of revenue. Management says 40% of the industry's work is "AI-disrupted" and can shrink 3-5% a year, 2-3% a year for HCLTech's mix, and that "very little" of it is in reported numbers yet. The same deal is ~20% smaller than before.

arguments.h: Margins, returns and cash are excellent
arguments.p: EBIT 17.5% in Q1FY27 before restructuring; ROIC 40.7% (Services 47.8%); free cash flow ~100% of net income; ₹26,900 cr net cash; at least 75% of profit returned by policy (90%+ in practice). We model EBIT of ₹{{F.ebit.0|num}} cr in FY27E, 17.7% of revenue, inside the 17.5-18.5% guidance.

arguments.h: The sector has been re-priced; HCLTech only partly
arguments.p: Eight Indian IT peers trade a median 34% below their five-year median P/E (TCS −53%, Infosys −49%); HCLTech −21%. At ₹1,230 it trades at 16.0x our FY28E EPS against 13x in our target. The street's median target is ₹1,225, flat on the price.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first test of whether the telecom cuts have bottomed; management said it would revisit FY27 guidance after Q2.
The US$1.14 bn mega deal: transition through H2FY27, steady state from April 2027 (management), the main support for FY28 growth.
AI data-centre plan: how much of the up-to-₹3,500 cr comes from HCLTech's balance sheet versus partners, clients and debt, and the returns it earns.
HCLSoftware: whether Jaspersoft (US$10-15 m a quarter) and the data portfolio stop the revenue decline; ARR has been flat near US$1.05 bn for two years.
New AI-model releases: Anthropic's tools triggered the February 2026 sell-offs; each new capability re-opens the deflation debate.

sections.title: Three businesses: IT services, engineering services and a software portfolio bought mostly from IBM

blocks.p: HCLTech sells technology work to large companies, mostly in the US (56% of Services revenue) and Europe (28%). It reports three segments. **IT & Business Services** (₹96,095 cr in FY26, 74% of revenue) runs and changes clients' systems: applications, cloud and data-centre infrastructure, digital workplace and networks, cybersecurity, back-office processes and, increasingly, AI and data work. It is strongest in long "managed services" contracts where HCLTech runs a client's infrastructure for five to ten years. **Engineering & R&D Services** (₹22,063 cr, 17%) designs products for technology, telecom, auto, medical-device and semiconductor companies: software, embedded systems, chips. **HCLSoftware** (₹12,397 cr, 9.5%) owns software products, largely acquired (select IBM products in 2019, Actian, Zeenea, Jaspersoft), sold mostly as subscriptions and support.

sections.title: A mature, slowing market that generative AI is re-pricing

blocks.p: Indian IT services companies earn most of their money from large US and European companies, doing work that is cheaper to do from India: building and maintaining software, running data centres and networks, back-office processing and engineering. For two decades the industry grew with outsourcing, then cloud and "digital" (2020-22). Since FY23 growth has slowed to low single digits in dollars: clients cut discretionary projects after the post-Covid boom, and from 2025 generative AI began to change what clients buy. AI tools write and test code, answer support tickets and monitor systems, so the same work needs fewer people. Most Indian IT contracts are priced on effort (people x time) or on fixed fees renegotiated every few years, so productivity gains flow to clients as lower prices.

sections.title: Cycle or lasting de-rating? Mostly lasting: AI is shrinking the work HCLTech is paid for, faster than new AI work replaces it

blocks.p: This is the question that decides the stock, and the whole sector. Indian IT shares fell hard in 2025-26: the Nifty IT index was ~25% down in 2026 by early June and ~29% below its late-2025 high (Analytics India Magazine, 9-Jun-2026). By 30-Sep-2026 eight listed IT peers traded a median 34% below their own five-year median P/E (TCS −53%, Infosys −49%, Wipro −40%); HCLTech −21%. Two explanations compete. The **cyclical** one: clients froze discretionary budgets because of tariffs, war in West Asia and an uncertain US economy, and spending will come back as it did after 2009 and 2020. The **structural** one: generative AI lets clients do the same work with far fewer people, and because Indian IT is paid largely for people and time, its revenue pool shrinks for good.

blocks.callout: **Our verdict: mostly lasting.** The client-specific cuts are cyclical and should fade by FY28. But three things are structural: (1) AI deflation is now visible in deal values (~20% smaller for the same scope) and in productivity give-backs, before most of it has reached revenue; (2) the AI-native work that grows fast is ~5% of revenue and adds ~1.4 pts of growth a year against 2-3 pts of deflation; (3) the people-based model that earned premium multiples for two decades is what AI compresses. We therefore forecast US$ growth of only ~3-4% a year even with the mega deal, hold EBIT margins flat near 18% (productivity goes to clients), and do **not** assume the sector re-rates: our 13x target multiple keeps the full 34% sector de-rating on HCLTech's 19.8x median. What would change our mind: two or three quarters of Services growth above 5% CC with stable pricing, or Advanced AI reaching ~10% of revenue while traditional revenue holds.

bullets: **What it is.** Applications, infrastructure and cloud, digital workplace, networks, cybersecurity, data and AI, and business-process work. ₹96,095 cr in FY26, up from ₹53,401 cr in FY21 (12.5% a year in rupees). Constant-currency growth was 3.7% in FY26 and 4.2% YoY in Q1FY27 (flat QoQ in a seasonally weak quarter).

**Margins.** Segment EBIT margin 17.9% (FY22), 16.6% (FY23), 17.0% (FY24), 17.1% (FY25), 16.0% (FY26, after most of the ~65 bp restructuring charge). Q1FY27 17% (+184 bp YoY): the restructuring is paying off and the rupee helps.

**Where the growth comes from.** Financial services (+5.3% in Q1), public services (+12%), retail (+10%), and large managed-services and modernisation deals; AI Force (HCLTech's delivery platform) is now in 92 accounts. **Where it is weak:** two large US telecom clients cut digital spend for CY2026, two SAP programmes were cancelled, and a retail client scaled back a platform build.

**The mega deal.** A Europe-headquartered Fortune Global 50 company chose HCLTech in early July 2026 to run its digital workplace and enterprise networks with AI (US$1.14 bn of new TCV per Equirus and PL). Transition starts in H2FY27; steady state in April 2027; "negligible" FY27 revenue (CEO).

**The AI exposure.** This is where most of the "AI-disrupted" work sits (application support, infrastructure operations, service desks). HCLTech's answer is to offer the productivity first ("proactive transformation"), accepting lower revenue per contract to win share.

Revenue US$1,395 m in FY26 (-4.1% CC): subscription & support US$1,190 m (85%), perpetual licences US$127 m (-29%), services US$78 m. Q1FY27 US$313 m (-5.3% YoY CC).

**Margins are high and lumpy.** Segment EBIT 23.7% (FY22) to 26.7% (FY26) on segment revenue; quarterly from 17.6% (Q1FY27) to 35.0% (Q3FY26) because licence renewals bunch in the December quarter. EBITDA is far higher: amortisation of acquired IP was ₹1,759 cr in FY23 (16% of segment revenue, the last year disclosed), and its run-off has propped up EBIT while revenue stalled.

**Why it shrinks.** Several products (in what management calls the "experience" portfolio) are mature and declining; government buyers prefer perpetual licences, which are unpredictable; management expects the data and operations portfolios to offset the decline and sees FY27 as "flattish or marginally declining".
**ROIC 21.6%** (Jun-2026, company measure) against 47.8% for Services: the IBM purchase earns its cost of capital but no more.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** HCLTech has a moat in execution, not in price. Clients trust it with very large, long contracts (23 accounts above US$100 m a year, renewals of its largest clients, mega deals executed "to the planned business case"), and its engineering franchise is the deepest among Indian tier-1s. But the moat that earned 20x+ multiples, cheap skilled labour delivered at scale, is what generative AI attacks. HCLTech's response (sell the productivity first, build AI platforms, buy software, invest in AI data centres) is sensible and early, yet it means accepting lower revenue per contract for a few years. HCLSoftware is a moat of sorts (customers rarely switch core software) but it protects a shrinking revenue base. We score the overall moat as narrow and narrowing.

sections.title: A decade of double-digit rupee growth; EPS has slowed to ~4% a year since FY23

blocks.p: HCLTech's revenue grew from ₹47,568 cr in FY17 to ₹1,30,144 cr in FY26, about 11.8% a year, helped by the IBM software purchase (2019), steady acquisitions and a weaker rupee. Profit attributable to shareholders went from ₹8,606 cr to ₹16,642 cr (7.6% a year). The last three years were slower: revenue grew 8.7% a year in rupees but only ~5% in dollars (FY24 +5.4%, FY25 +4.7%, FY26 +3.9% in constant currency), and EPS rose from ₹54.7 (FY23) to ₹61.3 (FY26), 3.9% a year. FY26 carried a ₹956 cr one-time charge for India's new Labour Codes and ~65 bp of restructuring; before them EPS was ₹64.0.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts and strong cash; watch the hedge book, the "one-offs" and acquisition accounting

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 120% of attributable profit in FY26, 128% in FY25 and 143% in FY24; the company's free cash flow was 107% of net income in FY26 and 99% on a twelve-month basis at Jun-2026. Cash from operations has exceeded profit every year since FY20 (FY18-19 were 89-96%).

**"One-offs" recur.** Restructuring cost ~65 bp of margin in FY26 and 62 bp in Q1FY27, and FY27 guidance includes another 40-50 bp: three years of "one-time" charges. The Labour Codes charge (₹956 cr, Q3FY26) is genuinely one-off, with a 10-20 bp recurring cost. We treat restructuring as an operating cost in FY27 and assume none after.

**Other income is mostly treasury.** FY26 other income ₹1,530 cr (company): interest and fund income ₹1,633 cr, other recurring items ₹138 cr, forex −₹241 cr. FY25's ₹2,485 cr included a ₹574 cr gain on divesting the State Street JV. Screener's FY26 figure (₹574 cr) nets the Labour Codes charge.

**Hedges.** A US$1.6 bn USD/INR forward book carried a ₹1,466 cr mark-to-market loss at Mar-2026 (hedging reserve −₹1,062 cr after tax), with hedged transactions running to Dec-2030; settlement losses go through the forex line. Not an accounting problem, but it dilutes the rupee benefit.

**Acquired IP.** About three-quarters of net fixed assets are goodwill (₹23,888 cr at Mar-2026) and other intangibles (~₹5,200 cr), mostly from the IBM software products, Actian and other deals. Amortisation runs through D&A, so EBIT is after it; we do not adjust it back.
**Pay.** CEO pay of US$18.1 m in FY26 (292x the median employee) and ₹131 cr of share-based pay for key managers: high for a company growing 4%.
**Disclosure.** Good on segments, verticals, geographies, clients, software ARR and Advanced AI; utilisation and segment D&A are no longer disclosed.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit by B S R & Co. LLP (re-appointed to 2029), strong cash conversion, net cash, clear segment reporting. The items to watch are the recurring "restructuring" line, the hedge losses as the rupee falls, and goodwill on the newer acquisitions (Jaspersoft, HPE Telco Solutions).

sections.title: Our honest summary: a quality company at a price that assumes AI is only a cycle; SELL at 16.0x FY28E

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's third-largest IT services company, best-in-class among tier-1s at winning large deals, with the deepest engineering franchise, a profitable (if shrinking) software arm, EBIT margins of ~18%, ROIC of ~40%, ₹26,900 cr of net cash and a policy of returning at least 75% of profit (90%+ in practice): a dividend yield of ~5.6% on our FY28E.

**What you are paying:** 17.0x our FY27E and 16.0x FY28E EPS for a business growing ~3-4% in dollars, in a sector the market has de-rated by ~34% for reasons we think are mostly lasting. assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for HCL Technologies (consolidated, Rs crore). Revenue is built in US dollars by reported segment (IT & Business Services, Engineering & R&D Services, HCLSoftware, less inter-segment sales), from constant-currency growth plus cross-currency moves and acquisitions, converted at a stated INR/USD path (usdBuild); the segment INR growth rates below are computed from that build. Segment margins are segment EBIT as HCLTech reports it (after allocated depreciation and amortisation; the sum of segment results equals Screener EBITDA less D&A in FY21-26). Because the engine builds EBITDA from segments, the unallocated line adds D&A back (negative cost) and the engine then deducts D&A computed on gross block: group EBIT = sum of segment EBIT, checked in HCLTECH.ctx.js. Profit is attributable to owners (Screener Net Profit replaced by Profit for EPS, tools/authoring/HCLTECH.patch.js); the tax line also carries the tiny minority share. Valued on P/E, as the street does.

usdBuild._note: US$ m. Base = FY26 segment revenue (AR FY26 note 3.30) / the FY26 implied rate of 88.75 (Rs130,144 cr / US$14,664 m reported); the bases sum to US$14,664 m. usdGrowth = ccGrowth + crossCurrency + acquisitions; inrGrowth = (1 + usdGrowth) x rate(t) / rate(t-1) - 1. HCLTech discloses revenue by segment only in rupees and as a % of US$ revenue; the US$ split is derived.
usdBuild._rateWhy: INR/USD averages: FY26 88.72 (quarterly 85.62 / 87.63 / 89.34 / 92.28, investor releases), Q1FY27 94.73. The rupee closed at 95.81 on 30-Sep-2026 (PTI). FY27E 95.53 = Q1 actual plus 95.81 for the remaining three quarters; FY28E-29E held at the 30-Sep spot of 95.81. We assume no further depreciation (history: ~3% a year over FY22-26, from 74.6 to 88.7): a 1% weaker rupee adds ~1% to revenue and, with ~60% of costs in rupees, ~2% to EPS. Motilal Oswal uses 94.5 / 95.0 for FY27E / FY28E (13-Jul-2026).

Cross-currency +0.1% in FY27 (GBP/EUR flat vs FY26 averages; Q1 +0.4 pt).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The AI shift turns out to be a cycle, not a shrink: discretionary spend returns in FY28, AI-native work (AI Factory, physical AI, chip engineering, sovereign AI) grows 30%+ and the data-centre bet adds a new line, so Services grow ~6-7% CC in FY28-29; HCLSoftware stabilises on data products; EBIT margin moves to the top of the 17.5-18.5% band.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: AI deflation runs faster than management's 2-3% (renewals re-priced 20-30% lower, more cost-take-out deals), the telecom and manufacturing cuts spread and Europe stays weak: US$ revenue grows ~0-1% a year; pricing pressure and AI investment push EBIT margin to ~16.5%, below the guided band; HCLSoftware keeps shrinking.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values HCLTech: P/E on FY28E or one-year-forward EPS (Motilal Oswal 18x, Geojit 19x, Equirus 16x Sep-28E, PL / ICICI Securities / HDFC 15x FY28E, Kotak 15x Jun-28E; Jun-Aug 2026). 13x = HCLTech's 19.8x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian; no trough years; 20.1x on EPS before the FY25 JV gain and FY26 Labour Codes charge) cut by the 34.5% median de-rating of eight Indian IT peers versus their five-year median P/E at 30-Sep-2026 (TCS -53%, Infosys -49%, Wipro -40%, LTIMindtree -38%, L&T Technology -31%, Mphasis -27%, Persistent -18%, Coforge -11%; Tech Mahindra left out because its trough-and-recovery earnings distort both its median and its current P/E; with it the median is -31%) = 13.0x. No further adjustment: our FY27-29E EPS growth (~5% a year after the rupee boost) is below the 8.4% of FY21-26, but that slowdown is what the sector de-rating prices; a dividend-discount check (90% payout, Ke 11.9%, 5% growth) also gives 13x. Bull 16x (half the de-rating reverses); bear 11x (the 44.5% median de-rating of the tier-1 peers TCS, Infosys, Wipro and LTIMindtree; also HCLTech's 2016-20 low of ~11x).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Counts net cash at face value. 7.7x Sep-28E EBITDA = HCLTech's 13.8x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, less the same 34.5% sector de-rating (9.0x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~18% above the twelve months to Jun-26 (Rs27,539 cr). Bull 9.7x / bear 6.5x on the same de-rating steps as the P/E.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 10-year FCFF, Ke 11.9%, terminal growth 5%, plus net cash.
